```{css, echo=FALSE}
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Café skin: cream paper, espresso ink, Starbucks green accents.
   Styling only - no data or logic lives in here.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,500;9..144,700&family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&display=swap');

:root {
  --cafe-cream:  #FBF7EE;
  --cafe-sand:   #F3ECDD;
  --cafe-tan:    #E2D5BB;
  --cafe-green:  #00704A;
  --cafe-forest: #1E3932;
  --cafe-mocha:  #9D5C3F;
  --cafe-ink:    #2B2723;
  --cafe-muted:  #6E665B;
}

body, .main-container {
  background-color: var(--cafe-cream);
  color: var(--cafe-ink);
  font-family: 'Inter', -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: 14.5px;
  line-height: 1.6;
}

h1, h2, h3, h4, h5,
.chart-title, .navbar-brand, .navbar-title {
  font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif;
  letter-spacing: 0.01em;
}

/* --- Navbar: dark roast green ------------------------------------- */
.navbar, .navbar-inverse, .navbar-default {
  background-color: var(--cafe-forest) !important;
  background-image: none !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  border-bottom: 3px solid var(--cafe-green) !important;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 14px -6px rgba(30, 57, 50, 0.55);
}
.navbar .navbar-brand, .navbar .navbar-title, .navbar-header .navbar-brand {
  color: var(--cafe-cream) !important;
  font-weight: 700;
  font-size: 19px;
}
.navbar-nav > li > a, .navbar .nav-link {
  color: rgba(251, 247, 238, 0.75) !important;
  font-size: 13px;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}
.navbar-nav > li.active > a,
.navbar-nav > li > a:hover,
.navbar .nav-link.active, .navbar .nav-link:hover {
  color: #FFFFFF !important;
  background-color: rgba(0, 112, 74, 0.55) !important;
  border-radius: 8px;
}

/* --- Cards: menu boards on cream paper ---------------------------- */
.chart-wrapper, .sbframe-commentary, .value-box {
  background-color: #FFFFFF;
  border: 1px solid var(--cafe-tan);
  border-radius: 14px;
  box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(30, 57, 50, 0.05),
              0 14px 28px -20px rgba(30, 57, 50, 0.35);
  margin: 9px;
}
.chart-wrapper .chart-title {
  background-color: #FFFFFF;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--cafe-sand);
  border-radius: 14px 14px 0 0;
  color: var(--cafe-forest);
  font-size: 14px;
  font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  padding: 13px 18px 11px;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}
.chart-stage, .chart-shim { padding: 6px 16px 14px; }

/* --- Sidebar: the chalkboard -------------------------------------- */
.section.sidebar {
  background-color: var(--cafe-sand);
  border-right: 1px solid var(--cafe-tan);
  color: var(--cafe-ink);
  font-size: 13.5px;
  line-height: 1.58;
  padding: 16px 20px;
}
.section.sidebar h3 {
  color: var(--cafe-forest);
  font-size: 16px;
  margin-top: 4px;
}
.section.sidebar strong { color: var(--cafe-mocha); }

/* --- Tabs --------------------------------------------------------- */
.nav-tabs {
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--cafe-tan);
  padding: 0 10px;
}
.nav-tabs > li > a, .nav-tabs .nav-link {
  border: 0 !important;
  color: var(--cafe-muted);
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
}
.nav-tabs > li.active > a, .nav-tabs .nav-link.active {
  background-color: transparent !important;
  border-bottom: 3px solid var(--cafe-green) !important;
  color: var(--cafe-forest) !important;
}

/* --- Type details ------------------------------------------------- */
a { color: var(--cafe-green); text-decoration: none; }
a:hover { color: var(--cafe-mocha); text-decoration: underline; }
hr { border-top: 1px solid var(--cafe-tan); }
blockquote {
  background-color: var(--cafe-sand);
  border-left: 4px solid var(--cafe-green);
  border-radius: 0 10px 10px 0;
  color: var(--cafe-forest);
  font-size: 14px;
  padding: 10px 16px;
}
ul { padding-left: 20px; }
li { margin-bottom: 3px; }
code, pre {
  background-color: var(--cafe-sand);
  border: 1px solid var(--cafe-tan);
  border-radius: 8px;
  color: var(--cafe-forest);
  font-family: 'SFMono-Regular', Consolas, Menlo, monospace;
  font-size: 12.5px;
}

/* --- Tables ------------------------------------------------------- */
.table, table {
  background-color: #FFFFFF;
  border-radius: 10px;
  font-size: 13.5px;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.table > tbody > tr:nth-of-type(odd), .table-striped tbody tr:nth-of-type(odd) {
  background-color: var(--cafe-cream);
}
.table > tbody > tr:hover, .table-hover tbody tr:hover {
  background-color: #EAF3EE !important;
}
caption, .table caption {
  color: var(--cafe-muted);
  font-size: 12.5px;
  font-style: italic;
  padding-bottom: 8px;
}

/* --- Gauges ------------------------------------------------------- */
.gauge .gauge-value, .gauge text { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif !important; }
```

```{r cafe_style, echo=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visual kit only: café palette + one shared ggplot theme.
# Nothing here reads, filters or computes data.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
cafe_cream   <- "#FBF7EE"
cafe_sand    <- "#F3ECDD"
cafe_tan     <- "#D8C7A6"
cafe_sage    <- "#8FB3A1"
cafe_green   <- "#00704A"
cafe_forest  <- "#1E3932"
cafe_caramel <- "#C58B49"
cafe_mocha   <- "#9D5C3F"
cafe_gold    <- "#C9A227"
cafe_ink     <- "#2B2723"
cafe_grey    <- "#6E665B"

# ramp for scales that need an arbitrary number of steps (e.g. cup sizes)
cafe_ramp <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(cafe_tan, cafe_sage, cafe_green, cafe_forest))

# milk colours, keyed two ways: by label and by the 0-5 code
milk_palette <- c(
  "No Milk"       = cafe_tan,
  "Nonfat Milk"   = cafe_sage,
  "2% Milk"       = cafe_green,
  "Soy Milk"      = cafe_caramel,
  "Coconut Milk"  = cafe_mocha,
  "Whole Milk"    = cafe_forest
)
milk_labels <- c("No Milk", "Nonfat", "2% Milk", "Soy", "Coconut", "Whole")
milk_codes  <- setNames(unname(milk_palette), as.character(0:5))

# tidy up nutrient labels on axes (display text only)
pretty_nutrient <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("^mean_", "", x)
  x <- gsub("_mg$", " (mg)", x)
  x <- gsub("_g$", " (g)", x)
  x <- gsub("_", " ", x)
  tools::toTitleCase(x)
}

theme_cafe <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text             = element_text(colour = cafe_ink),
      plot.title       = element_text(colour = cafe_forest, face = "bold",
                                      size = base_size + 2, hjust = 0,
                                      margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = cafe_mocha, size = base_size - 1.5,
                                      margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.caption     = element_text(colour = cafe_grey, size = base_size - 4, hjust = 0),
      axis.title       = element_text(colour = cafe_forest, size = base_size - 1.5),
      axis.text        = element_text(colour = cafe_grey, size = base_size - 2.5),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#E7DFD0", linewidth = 0.35),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      legend.title     = element_text(colour = cafe_forest, size = base_size - 2.5),
      legend.text      = element_text(colour = cafe_grey, size = base_size - 2.5),
      plot.margin      = margin(12, 16, 8, 12)
    )
}
```

```{r read_sbux_data, message = FALSE, include=FALSE}
starbucks <- read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2021/2021-12-21/starbucks.csv')
```

```{r making everything into double, echo=FALSE}

starbucks$trans_fat_g <- as.double(starbucks$trans_fat_g)
starbucks$fiber_g <- as.double(starbucks$fiber_g)

```

```{r finding means, echo=FALSE}
starbucks_means <- starbucks %>%
  summarize(
    mean_calories = mean(calories),
    mean_fat = mean(total_fat_g),
    mean_saturated_fat = mean(saturated_fat_g),
    mean_trans_fat = mean(trans_fat_g), 
    mean_cholesterol = mean(cholesterol_mg),
    mean_sodium = mean(sodium_mg),
    mean_carbs = mean(total_carbs_g),
    mean_fiber = mean(fiber_g),
    mean_sugar = mean(sugar_g))

```

```{r seperating each milk}

milk_no <- starbucks %>% filter(milk == 0)
milk_nonfat <- starbucks %>% filter(milk == 1)
milk_2 <- starbucks %>% filter(milk == 2)
milk_soy <- starbucks %>% filter(milk == 3)
milk_coconut <- starbucks %>% filter(milk == 4)
milk_whole <- starbucks %>% filter(milk == 5)
```


The Counter {data-icon="ion-coffee"}
=====================================

Column {data-width=640}
-------------------------------------

### Pull up a chair

**What is in the cup, really?**

Every drink on the Starbucks board carries a nutrition panel that almost nobody reads. This dashboard gives a summar of it [the full menu table](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/master/data/2021/2021-12-21/readme.md#starbucks) lists each drink with its size, its milk, its caffeine and the rest of its numbers.

Nothing here is a recommendation. It is just the menu, with an extra analysis to it.

***

Column {data-width=360}
-------------------------------------

### Today's tasting flight

**1 · First Pour**  
Break down the drinks! Which styles dominate?

**2 · Whipped Cream**  
Does that swirl on top track with the sugar in the cup?

**3 · Milk or No Milk**  
What separates a drink with milk from one without, nutrient by nutrient?

**4 · The Milk Bar**  
Nonfat, 2%, soy, coconut, whole, does the choice of milk change the panel?

**5 · Caffeine Hit**  
How do caffeinated drinks compare with the decaf side of the board, and does caffeine actually help explain calories?

### From the roastery

The numbers come from the TidyTuesday release of the Starbucks drinks menu: one row per drink per size, with serving size, milk code, whipped-cream flag, caffeine and the full nutrition panel.


First Pour {data-icon="ion-pie-graph" data-orientation=rows}
=====================================

Row {data-height=215}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Drinks poured with milk

```{r}
total_drinks <- nrow(starbucks)
drinks_with_milk <- nrow(starbucks %>% filter(milk != 0))

percentage_w_milk <- (drinks_with_milk / total_drinks) * 100

gauge_chart <- gauge(percentage_w_milk, min = 0, max = 100, symbol = '%',
                     gaugeSectors(success = c(0, 100),
                                  colors = c(cafe_green, cafe_gold, cafe_mocha)))
gauge_chart

```

### Drinks with caffeine

```{r}

drinks_with_caffeine <- nrow(starbucks %>% filter(caffeine_mg > 0))

percentage_w_caffeine <- (drinks_with_caffeine / total_drinks) * 100

# sector colours only - espresso green up top, caramel in the middle band
gauge_chart <- gauge(percentage_w_caffeine, min = 0, max = 100, symbol = '%',
                     gaugeSectors(success = c(0, 100),
                                  colors = c(cafe_forest, cafe_gold, cafe_mocha)))

gauge_chart

```

### Reading the two dials

- **85.6%** of the board is poured with some kind of milk
- **86.6%** of the board carries caffeine
- So nearly every drink on the menu is a milk drink, a caffeine drink, or both

Row {data-height=500 .tabset .tabset-fade}
-------------------------------------

### Milk on the board

```{r graph of beverage with different milk types}


counting_by_milk <- rbind(
  data.frame(MilkType = "No Milk", Count = nrow(milk_no)),
  data.frame(MilkType = "Nonfat Milk", Count = nrow(milk_nonfat)),
  data.frame(MilkType = "2% Milk", Count = nrow(milk_2)),
  data.frame(MilkType = "Soy Milk", Count = nrow(milk_soy)),
  data.frame(MilkType = "Coconut Milk", Count = nrow(milk_coconut)),
  data.frame(MilkType = "Whole Milk", Count = nrow(milk_whole))
)

#make graph (use identity)
graph_milk_count <- ggplot(counting_by_milk, aes(x = MilkType,
                             y = Count, 
                             fill = MilkType)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.68) +
  labs(title = "Drinks on the board, by milk",
       subtitle = "Nonfat milk carries most of the menu",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_cafe() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = milk_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = "Milk Type", y = "Count")

ggplotly(graph_milk_count)

```  
 

### Caffeine split 
 
 
```{r}

drinks_with_caffeine <- nrow(starbucks %>% filter(caffeine_mg > 0))
drinks_without_caffeine <- nrow(starbucks %>% filter(caffeine_mg == 0))

numbers_drinks_caffeine <- c(drinks_with_caffeine, drinks_without_caffeine)
labels <- c("Caffeine", "Non-Caffeine")

colors <- c(cafe_forest, cafe_tan)

par(bg = NA, mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), family = "sans")

pie(numbers_drinks_caffeine, labels = labels, col = colors,
    border = "#FFFFFF", lwd = 2, clockwise = TRUE, init.angle = 90,
    cex = 0.95, col.main = cafe_forest)

legend("topright", legend = labels, fill = colors, bty = "n",
       border = "#FFFFFF", cex = 0.9, text.col = cafe_ink)

title("Caffeinated vs. decaf", col.main = cafe_forest, font.main = 2, cex.main = 1.15)


```

### Cup sizes 

```{r table for sizes}

beverage_data_sizes <- starbucks %>%
  group_by(size) %>%
  summarise('average serving size' = mean(serv_size_m_l))%>%
  arrange(desc(`average serving size`))

size_info <- beverage_data_sizes %>%
  kable(caption = "Average pour per cup size, biggest first",
        col.names = c("Cup size", "Average serving (mL)"),
        digits = 1,
        align = c("l", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("hover", "striped", "condensed"),
                full_width = TRUE,
                font_size = 13) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = cafe_cream, background = cafe_forest)

size_info

```



```{r sizes difference}

counting_by_size <- starbucks %>%
  group_by(size) %>%
  summarise(Count = sum(n()))

result_q1_sizes <- ggplot(counting_by_size, aes(x = size, y = Count, fill = size)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "How many drinks come in each size",
       subtitle = "Grande, venti and tall carry the menu; the tiny sizes are add-ons",
       x = "Size", y = "Count") +
  theme_cafe() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cafe_ramp(nrow(counting_by_size))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)))

ggplotly(result_q1_sizes)


```


Whipped Cream {data-icon="ion-ice-cream"}
=====================================

Column {.sidebar data-width=380}
-----
### The swirl on top

Side by side, the box plots lean the same way: drinks finished with whipped cream sit at a **higher average sugar** level. Both groups spread widely, though, so the cream is not the whole story.


Row
-----
### Sugar in the cup, with and without the whip

```{r graph whip n sugar}

drinks_whip <- starbucks %>% filter(whip == 1 )
drinks_no_whip <- starbucks %>% filter(whip == 0)

whip_no_whip <- rbind(drinks_whip, drinks_no_whip)


whip_no_whip <- whip_no_whip %>% select(whip, sugar_g) 


whip_no_whip <- whip_no_whip %>%
  mutate(whip = case_when(
    whip == 0 ~ "No Whipcream",
    whip == 1 ~ "Whipcream"))


sugar_drinks_whip <- ggplot(whip_no_whip, aes(x = whip, y = sugar_g, fill = whip)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, colour = cafe_forest, outlier.colour = cafe_mocha,
               outlier.alpha = 0.55, outlier.size = 1.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Whipped cream and sugar, side by side",
    subtitle = "Each box covers the middle half of the drinks in that group",
    y = "Sugar (g)",
    x = "Whipped cream"
  ) +
  theme_cafe() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = 1), legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Whipcream" = cafe_caramel, "No Whipcream" = cafe_sage))

ggplotly(sugar_drinks_whip)


```



Milk or No Milk {data-icon="ion-beaker"}
=====================================

Row
-------------------------------------

### Nutrient by nutrient

```{r graph nutrition of milk n no  milk}

beverages_with_milk <- starbucks %>% filter(milk == 0)
beverages_without_milk <- starbucks %>% filter(milk != 0)


nutritional_variables <- c("calories", "total_fat_g", "saturated_fat_g", "trans_fat_g", "cholesterol_mg", "sodium_mg", "total_carbs_g", "fiber_g", "sugar_g")

combined_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(BeverageType = "With Milk", beverages_with_milk[, nutritional_variables]),
  data.frame(BeverageType = "Without Milk", beverages_without_milk[, nutritional_variables]))

combined_data_long <- gather(combined_data, NutritionalVariable, Value, nutritional_variables)


milk_vs_nonmilk <- ggplot(combined_data_long, aes(x = NutritionalVariable, y = Value, fill = BeverageType)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.72) +
  labs(title = "Milk drinks against milk-free drinks",
       subtitle = "Same nutrition panel, two different halves of the menu",
       x = "Nutrient",
       y = "Value") +
  theme_cafe() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
        legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = pretty_nutrient) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("With Milk" = cafe_green, "Without Milk" = cafe_tan))

ggplotly(milk_vs_nonmilk)

```

Column {.sidebar data-width=380}
---------
### Milk pulls its weight

Line the two groups up and the milk drinks sit higher almost everywhere — calories, cholesterol, fibre, saturated fat, sodium, sugar, total carbohydrate and total fat.

Whatever else goes into the cup, **milk is doing much of the heavy lifting on the nutrition panel.**


The Milk Bar {data-icon="ion-stats-bars"}
=====================================

Column {.sidebar data-width=400}
-------------------------------------
### Chalkboard notes

Across every chart on this page, the milk you pick leaves a mark. No-milk drinks sit lowest, and the different milks shuffle the panel in their own small ways.

**1 · Calories**

- Whole milk tops the calorie count on average.
- The gaps between milks stay modest, so the effect is steady rather than dramatic.

**2 · Total fat**

- Same story as calories: whole milk leads.
- Fat moves little from one milk to the next.

**3 · Saturated fat**

- Coconut milk sits highest here, with whole milk just behind.

**4 · Trans fat**

- Tiny either way. Whichever milk goes in, trans fat stays near zero next to the other nutrients.

**5 · Cholesterol**

- Whole milk leads again.
- Soy and coconut come in lowest, well under the dairy options.

**6 · Sodium**

- No-milk drinks are very low; anything with milk jumps up.
- Between the milks, sodium barely moves.

**7 · Carbohydrate**

- Little variation from one milk to the next.

**8 · Fibre**

- Most milk drinks land between 0 g and 1 g.
- Soy is the outlier, carrying noticeably more fibre than the rest.

**9 · Sugar**

- 2% and whole milk average the same sugar.
- Chasing less sugar? The no-milk side of the board is the safer bet.

```{r average nutrition table by milk}

mean_nutrition_by_milk <- starbucks %>%
  group_by(milk) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(nutritional_variables), ~mean(.), .names = "mean_{.col}"))

mean_nutrition_by_milk$milk <- as.character(mean_nutrition_by_milk$milk)
```


### Calories


```{r graph calorie by milk}

cal_milk <- ggplot(mean_nutrition_by_milk, aes(x = milk, y = mean_calories, fill = milk)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.68) +
  labs(title = "Average calories by milk",
       subtitle = "Whole milk sits on top, but the spread is narrow") +
  theme_cafe() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = "Milk Type", y = "Calories") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = milk_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = milk_codes, name = "Milk Type", labels = milk_labels) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_calories)),
            vjust = -0.6, size = 3.4, colour = cafe_forest, fontface = "bold")

ggplotly(cal_milk)


```

### Total fat

```{r graph fat by milk}
  labs(x = "Milk Type", y = "Fat (g)") +

  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_total_fat_g)),

ggplotly(fat_milk)
```

### Saturated fat

```{r graph saturated by milk}


sat_fat_milk <- ggplot(mean_nutrition_by_milk, aes(x = milk, y = mean_saturated_fat_g, fill = milk)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.68) +
  labs(title = "Average saturated fat by milk",
       subtitle = "Coconut leads, whole milk follows") +
  theme_cafe() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = "Milk Type", y = "Saturated fat (g)") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = milk_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = milk_codes, name = "Milk Type", labels = milk_labels) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_saturated_fat_g)),
            vjust = -0.6, size = 3.4, colour = cafe_forest, fontface = "bold")

ggplotly(sat_fat_milk)
```

Caffeine Hit {data-icon="ion-flash"}
=====================================

Column {.sidebar data-width=380}
-------------------------------------
### Chalkboard notes

- Caffeinated drinks generally carry **less** of everything on the panel, with fibre being the exception.
- Calories and sodium show the widest gap between the two sides of the board.
- Fit a straight line through calories against caffeine and the slope points gently downhill, so caffeine on its own explains very little of what ends up in the cup.

Row {.tabset .tabset-fade data-height=600}
---------

### Panel comparison

```{r,echo=FALSE}

caffeinated_drinks <- starbucks %>% filter(caffeine_mg > 0)
decaffeinated_drinks <- starbucks %>% filter(caffeine_mg == 0)

mean_nutrition_caffeinated <- caffeinated_drinks %>%
  summarize(
    mean_calories = mean(calories),
    mean_total_fat = mean(total_fat_g),
    mean_saturated_fat = mean(saturated_fat_g),
    mean_trans_fat = mean(trans_fat_g),
    mean_cholesterol = mean(cholesterol_mg),
    mean_sodium = mean(sodium_mg),
    mean_total_carbs = mean(total_carbs_g),
    mean_fiber = mean(fiber_g),
    mean_sugar = mean(sugar_g)
  )

mean_nutrition_decaffeinated <- decaffeinated_drinks %>%
  summarize(
    mean_calories = mean(calories),
    mean_total_fat = mean(total_fat_g),
    mean_saturated_fat = mean(saturated_fat_g),
    mean_trans_fat = mean(trans_fat_g),
    mean_cholesterol = mean(cholesterol_mg),
    mean_sodium = mean(sodium_mg),
    mean_total_carbs = mean(total_carbs_g),
    mean_fiber = mean(fiber_g),
    mean_sugar = mean(sugar_g)
  )
  


```



```{r graph caffeine vs non-caffeine}
mean_nutrition <- rbind(mean_nutrition_caffeinated, mean_nutrition_decaffeinated)
mean_nutrition$Caffeine <- c("Caffeinated", "Decaffeinated")

mean_nutrition_long <- gather(mean_nutrition, Nutrient, Mean_Value, -Caffeine)

caffeine_nutrition <- ggplot(mean_nutrition_long, aes(x = Nutrient, y = Mean_Value, fill = Caffeine)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.72) +
  labs(
    title = "Caffeinated against decaf, nutrient by nutrient",
    subtitle = "Average value per drink",
    y = "Average value",
    x = "Nutrient"
  ) +
  theme_cafe() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = pretty_nutrient) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Caffeinated" = cafe_forest,
                               "Decaffeinated" = cafe_caramel)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))

ggplotly(caffeine_nutrition)

```


### Caffeine against calories

```{r linear model}

caffeine_analysis <- rbind(caffeinated_drinks, decaffeinated_drinks)


lm_model <- lm(calories ~ caffeine_mg, data = caffeine_analysis)


summary(lm_model)


```

> **Reading the line**

- Setting up the fit:

  * The board is split in two — drinks with caffeine and drinks without.
  * The line then asks whether caffeine moves calories at all.

* Pearson correlation coefficient(r) = 0.0746

* Linear Model Information:

  * Intercept = 240.46421
  * Estimates using calories = -0.05241
  * $$\widehat{\text{Calories}} = 240.46421 - -0.13141~\text{Caffeine Content} + \widehat{\epsilon}$$

***



Last Sip {data-icon="ion-checkmark-round"}
=====================================

Column {data-width=620}
-------------------------------------

### What the menu gives up

**Five things worth remembering:**

**1 · Almost nothing is plain.**  
More than 80% of the board comes with milk, caffeine, or both.

**2 · The whip shows up in the sugar.**  
Drinks finished with whipped cream average more sugar than those without.

**3 · Milk lifts the whole panel.**  
Calories, trans fat, saturated fat, total fat, sodium, sugar, fibre, cholesterol and carbohydrate all sit higher in milk drinks.

**4 · Which milk matters too.**  
Every milk leaves its own mark — coconut on saturated fat, soy on fibre, whole milk on calories and cholesterol.

**5 · Caffeine is not the culprit.**  
Decaf drinks run higher on most of the panel, fibre aside. Calories and caffeine even lean slightly against each other: more caffeine, marginally fewer predicted calories.

Column {data-width=380}
-------------------------------------

### Ordering with this in mind

If the goal is a lighter cup, the levers are the ones the menu hands you at the register: **skip the whip, go lighter on the milk( or skip it) — and don't count on decaf being the gentler choice.**

***

Caffeine barely budges the calorie line, so the espresso shot is rarely what makes a drink heavy. The milk and the sugar get there first.
